summary: Purna Harsha Bajracharya worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1972, he was attested as Chief Research Officer at both the Archaeological Survey of India and the Department of Archaeology.

Purnima Dhavan is an historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Virginia. She taught at Bowdoin College and St. John's University before becoming Associate Professor of History at the University of Washington in 2005.

Purushottam Mahadev Joshi (1904–1989) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the University of Mumbai Library from circa 1935 to 1947 and as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat (1894–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning degrees from the University of Mumbai and Harvard University, he held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Purushottama Bilimoria, a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed a PhD at La Trobe University. He held positions at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, Stony Brook, Columbia, and UC Berkeley.

Pushpendra Kumar (b. 1936) is an Indologist who studied under Satya Vrat Shastri. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 1976) and as Principal of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891–1973) was an Indology scholar and retired judge of the Chief Court of Cochin. He also served as the president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at King's College London by 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow in 2017.

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, he held posts at Oxford, All Souls College, and Eötvös Loránd University.
Qian Cao is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. As of 2026, they are attested as both a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology, holding degrees from Fudan, Bristol, and Washington. She studied under Rupert Gethin, Richard Salomon, and Collett Cox, and was affiliated with the Hebrew University of Jerusalem as of 2026.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who completed doctoral studies under Hung Wu and Irene Winter. He held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and was a researcher at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) was a sinologist and historian who studied under Youwei Kang. He held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China.

Qing Duan (1953–2022) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies scholar. Educated at Peking University and the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, she served as a professor at Peking University from circa 1987 to 2022.

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) was a Tibetologist and historian educated at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He taught at Qinghai Nationalities University and directed the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center.
Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has held professorial posts at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University in 2013 under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.
R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras from circa 1974 to 1990.

R. D. Vadekar (1902–1986) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).
